regimens.indication: Empiric Bacterial Meningitis and MRSA/PRSP CNS Infections

refs.quote: indicated for the treatment of serious or severe infections caused by susceptible strains of methicillin-resistant (β-lactam-resistant) staphylococci.
Vancomycin does not readily diffuse across normal meninges into the spinal fluid; but, when the meninges are inflamed, penetration into the spinal fluid occurs.
usual daily intravenous dose is 2 g divided either as 500 mg every 6 hours or 1 g every 12 hours.

dose.frequency: every 8 to 12 hours (target AUC/MIC 400-600 or trough 15-20 mcg/mL); infuse at <= 10 mg/min

regimens.dose_text: 15 to 20 mg/kg IV every 8 to 12 hours (usual initial adult dose 1 g to 1.5 g IV every 12 hours). Administer by IV infusion over at least 60 minutes at a rate not exceeding 10 mg/min to prevent infusion-related reactions (red man syndrome). Therapeutic drug monitoring required: target AUC/MIC 400 to 600 or trough 15 to 20 mcg/mL.

regimens.indication: Serious or Severe MRSA and Susceptible Gram-Positive Infections (Septicemia, Bone, Lower Respiratory Tract, Skin and Skin Structure) — Adults

refs.quote: Vancomycin Hydrochloride for Injection, USP is effective in the treatment of staphylococcal endocarditis. Its effectiveness has been documented in other infections due to staphylococci, including septicemia, bone infections, lower respiratory tract infections, skin and skin structure infections.

The usual daily intravenous dose is 2 g divided either as 500 mg every 6 hours or 1 g every 12 hours. Each dose should be administered at no more than 10 mg/min or over a period of at least 60 minutes, whichever is longer.

dose.frequency: every 6 hours (or 1 g every 12 hours; usual daily dose 2 g)

regimens.dose_text: Usual daily IV dose is 2 g divided either as 500 mg every 6 hours or 1 g every 12 hours. Infuse at <=10 mg/min or over at least 60 minutes (whichever is longer), at a concentration <=5 mg/mL (up to 10 mg/mL only in fluid-restricted patients).

regimens.indication: Bacterial Endocarditis (Staphylococcal, S. viridans, S. bovis, Enterococcal, Diphtheroid, Prosthetic Valve) — Adults

refs.quote: Vancomycin Hydrochloride for Injection, USP has been reported to be effective alone or in combination with an aminoglycoside for endocarditis caused by S. viridans or S. bovis. For endocarditis caused by enterococci (e.g., E. faecalis), vancomycin has been reported to be effective only in combination with an aminoglycoside.

The usual daily intravenous dose is 2 g divided either as 500 mg every 6 hours or 1 g every 12 hours. Each dose should be administered at no more than 10 mg/min or over a period of at least 60 minutes, whichever is longer.

dose.frequency: every 12 hours (or 500 mg every 6 hours; combine with aminoglycoside for enterococci, and rifampin/aminoglycoside for early-onset prosthetic valve endocarditis)

regimens.dose_text: Usual adult IV dose 2 g/day divided as 500 mg every 6 hours or 1 g every 12 hours, infused at <=10 mg/min over >=60 minutes. Effective alone or with an aminoglycoside for S. viridans or S. bovis; only with an aminoglycoside for enterococci (e.g., E. faecalis); with rifampin, an aminoglycoside, or both for early-onset prosthetic valve endocarditis due to S. epidermidis or diphtheroids.

refs.quote: Pediatric patients The usual intravenous dosage of vancomycin is 10 mg/kg per dose given every 6 hours. Each dose should be administered over a period of at least 60 minutes.

regimens.dose_text: 10 mg/kg IV per dose given every 6 hours; administer each dose over at least 60 minutes. Close monitoring of serum vancomycin concentrations may be warranted.

regimens.dose_text: Initial dose of 15 mg/kg IV, followed by 10 mg/kg IV every 12 hours during the 1st week of life. Administer each dose over 60 minutes. Longer dosing intervals may be necessary in premature infants; monitor serum concentrations closely.

regimens.dose_text: Initial dose of 15 mg/kg IV, followed by 10 mg/kg IV every 8 hours from after the 1st week of life up to 1 month of age. Administer each dose over 60 minutes. Longer dosing intervals may be necessary in premature infants; monitor serum concentrations closely.

regimens.indication: Serious or Severe Gram-Positive Infections in Impaired Renal Function or Anuria — Adults

refs.quote: The initial dose should be no less than 15 mg/kg, even in patients with mild to moderate renal insufficiency. The table is not valid for functionally anephric patients. For such patients, an initial dose of 15 mg/kg of body weight should be given to achieve prompt therapeutic serum concentrations.

The dose required to maintain stable concentrations is 1.9 mg/kg/24 hr. In patients with marked renal impairment, it may be more convenient to give maintenance doses of 250 to 1,000 mg once every several days rather than administering the drug on a daily basis. In anuria, a dose of 1,000 mg every 7 to 10 days has been recommended.

dose.frequency: initial dose, then renal-adjusted maintenance (approx. 15 mg/day per mL/min GFR, or 1.9 mg/kg/24 hr in anephric patients)

regimens.dose_text: Initial dose >=15 mg/kg IV (even in mild-to-moderate renal insufficiency or functionally anephric patients). Maintenance: ~15 mg/day per mL/min CrCl (Moellering table: 155 mg/24h at CrCl 10 mL/min up to 1,545 mg/24h at CrCl 100 mL/min). In functionally anephric patients: 1.9 mg/kg/24h, or 250-1,000 mg every several days; in anuria: 1,000 mg every 7 to 10 days.

tier.note: No animal reproduction studies; limited 2nd/3rd-trimester human study showed cord blood transfer without drug-attributable sensorineural hearing loss or nephrotoxicity, so use only if clearly needed.

refs.quote: Because the number of patients treated in this study was limited and vancomycin was administered only in the second and third trimesters, it is not known whether vancomycin causes fetal harm. Vancomycin should be given to a pregnant woman only if clearly needed.

refs.quote: Vancomycin was found in cord blood. No sensorineural hearing loss or nephrotoxicity attributable to vancomycin was noted.

lactation_summary.value: Excreted in human milk; exercise caution when administering to a nursing woman and decide whether to discontinue nursing or the drug.

refs.quote: Vancomycin hydrochloride for injection is excreted in human milk. Caution should be exercised when vancomycin hydrochloride for injection is administered to a nursing woman. Because of the potential for adverse events, a decision should be made whether to discontinue nursing or to discontinue the drug, taking into account the importance of the drug to the mother.

value: Infusion-related reactions ('Red Man Syndrome'): flushing of upper body/neck, pruritus, erythema, urticaria, chills (rate-dependent; prevent by infusing <=10 mg/min or over >=60 min)
Injection site thrombophlebitis and local pain

refs.quote: Infusion-Related Events During or soon after rapid infusion of vancomycin hydrochloride for injection, patients may develop anaphylactoid reactions, including hypotension (see ANIMAL PHARMACOLOGY ), wheezing, dyspnea, urticaria, or pruritus.

value: Nephrotoxicity and Acute Kidney Injury (AKI; dose- and trough-dependent, significantly increased with AUC >600 mg*h/L, troughs >20 mcg/mL, or concomitant nephrotoxic agents like aminoglycosides, piperacillin-tazobactam, NSAIDs; monitor AUC/MIC or troughs)
Ototoxicity (sensorineural hearing loss, tinnitus, vertigo; may be permanent; risk increased with high serum concentrations or concomitant ototoxic drugs)
Severe anaphylaxis and hypotension / cardiovascular collapse during rapid infusion
Severe cutaneous adverse reactions: DRESS syndrome, Stevens-Johnson syndrome, linear IgA bullous dermatosis
Neutropenia (reversible on cessation; periodic CBC monitoring for prolonged courses >1-2 weeks)

refs.quote: Nephrotoxicity Systemic vancomycin exposure may result in acute kidney injury (AKI). The risk of AKI increases as systemic exposure/serum levels increase.

value.drug_or_class: Nephrotoxic and Ototoxic Agents (Aminoglycosides, Amphotericin B, Polymyxin B, Cisplatin)
value.effect: Additive or synergistic nephrotoxicity and eighth-cranial-nerve ototoxicity with concurrent or sequential systemic administration.
value.management: Monitor renal function (serum creatinine, eGFR) and vancomycin trough concentrations frequently; avoid combinations when feasible.

refs.quote: Monitor renal function in patients receiving vancomycin and concurrent and/or sequential systemic or topical use of other potentially, neurotoxic and/or nephrotoxic drugs, such as amphotericin B, aminoglycosides, bacitracin, polymyxin B, colistin, viomycin, or cisplatin.

value.effect: Concomitant administration has been associated with erythema, histamine-like flushing, and anaphylactoid reactions.
value.management: Infuse vancomycin over at least 60 minutes prior to anesthetic induction to minimize histamine-mediated infusion reactions.

refs.quote: Concomitant administration of vancomycin and anesthetic agents has been associated with erythema and histamine-like flushing (see Pediatric Use, PRECAUTIONS ) and anaphylactoid reactions (see ADVERSE REACTIONS ).

Monitor renal function in patients receiving vancomycin and concurrent and/or sequential systemic or topical use of other potentially, neurotoxic and/or nephrotoxic drugs, such as amphotericin B, aminoglycosides, bacitracin, polymyxin B, colistin, viomycin, or cisplatin.
